core.title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework for Autonomous Topology Optimization
core.abstract: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage.

sections.title: 从问题描述到优化结果，人工衔接仍是瓶颈
paragraphs: 拓扑优化已用于航空航天、汽车和机械工程，但提出一个新问题，并不意味着能够顺畅获得优化结果。摘要指出，现有流程涉及多个需要人工连接的环节，新问题往往需要手动编写和调试求解器代码，代码还可能运行失败或给出错误结果。
因此，本文关注的不只是生成代码，而是如何降低整个流程对专家操作的依赖。**代码能够运行与结果正确并非同一件事**，这也是理解其验证导向设计的重要切入点。

core.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications and Development in the Field of Electronic Test Instruments
core.venue: International Journal of Advanced Engineering and Technology Research
core.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), especially the fast iteration and widespread deployment of large language models (LLMs), has ushered in a new paradigm for the intelligent augmentation of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems (ATS). By combining the powerful reasoning and generative capabilities of LLMs with the timeliness and accuracy of external knowledge bases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a highly promising approach to addressing knowledge-intensive challenges in the operation and maintenance of electronic test instruments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of RAG and its applications in the field of electronic test instruments. First, the basic architecture of RAG is reviewed, including retrieval mechanisms, knowledge-base construction, and generative models. Then, considering the operational characteristics of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems, key knowledge-intensive tasks are analyzed, such as fault diagnosis, test configuration, and process planning, followed by a discussion of representative RAG-based applications, including intelligent fault diagnosis systems, adaptive test-parameter configuration, and interactive question-answering assistants. In addition, practical considerations for engineering implementation are discussed with respect to knowledge-base construction and effectiveness evaluation. Finally, open issues and future research directions are outlined, including multimodal RAG, federated learning for distributed knowledge bases, and edge deployment. This review aims to provide researchers and practitioners in relevant industries with a comprehensive understanding of the current status and development prospects of RAG technologies in electronic test instruments.

core.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
core.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

core.title: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Systems: A Review of Methods, Benchmarks, Challenges and Future Directions
core.venue: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports
core.abstract: Aims: To critically review how machine learning is applied to predictive maintenance of industrial assets, to compare the main method families and benchmark practices, and to identify the barriers that limit industrial adoption and the priorities for future research. Study Design: Narrative (non-systematic) review. Methodology: Peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers and established review studies published between 2006 and 2026 were identified from major scientific databases and publisher platforms using combinations of the terms predictive maintenance, condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, prognostics, remaining useful life and machine learning. Seminal and highly cited works, benchmark-dataset papers and recent advances were prioritised. The evidence was synthesised by maintenance task, method family, dataset, evaluation metric and deployment issue. Results: Machine learning in predictive maintenance has progressed from feature-engineered shallow classifiers to deep convolutional, recurrent and attention-based networks that learn directly from raw sensor signals, and, more recently, to transfer learning, federated learning, physics-informed hybrid models and large foundation models. Deep models report strong accuracy on public benchmarks for bearing fault diagnosis and turbofan remaining-useful-life estimation, and hybrid physics and deep-learning models have extended prognostic horizons while requiring less training data. However, most evidence comes from a small number of laboratory or simulated datasets; performance under domain shift, scarce failure data, uncertainty quantification, interpretability and the link between prediction and maintenance decisions remain weakly addressed. Conclusion: Machine learning is a mature enabler of predictive maintenance, but industrial value depends less on marginal benchmark gains than on robust, explainable, uncertainty-aware and decision-oriented models validated on field data. Standardised evaluation protocols, open industrial datasets, hybrid knowledge-and-data models and cost-benefit evidence are the main priorities for future work.

core.title: Thermal-Hydraulic Machine-Learning Surrogate Modeling for Structural Optimization of an Electric-Vehicle Battery Thermal Management System
core.abstract: Abstract Structural design of battery thermal management systems requires prediction of maximum temperature, maximum temperature difference, and pressure drop, whose scales and response forms differ. Direct multioutput regression overlooks response differences and the data support of optimized designs. This study develops a response-aligned machine-learning surrogate coupled with coverage-constrained multi-objective optimization and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation. Screening ten regressors identifies Extra Trees as the thermal baseline and a multilayer perceptron for pressure drop. Nested fivefold cross-validation repeated over five seeds selects direct Extra Trees for maximum temperature, log-response Extra Trees for maximum temperature difference, and velocity-normalized pressure-drop reconstruction with a multilayer perceptron. A label-independent sampling rule adds 40 designs to the 80-sample modeling set, while a disjoint 40-design holdout evaluates the deterministic distributed thermal network (DTN) mapping. On this holdout, the log-response and velocity-normalized branches reduce root mean squared error by 10.48% and 24.76%, respectively; the 95% paired-bootstrap interval confirms the pressure-drop improvement. Nominal 90% cross-validation-plus intervals achieve empirical coverages of 87.5%, 90.0%, and 100% for the three outputs. Across resamples, contact-length ratio remains the highest-ranked thermal feature, and local parameter sweeps reproduce the DTN trends. papers.title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework for Autonomous Topology Optimization
papers.abstract: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications and Development in the Field of Electronic Test Instruments
papers.venue: International Journal of Advanced Engineering and Technology Research
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), especially the fast iteration and widespread deployment of large language models (LLMs), has ushered in a new paradigm for the intelligent augmentation of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems (ATS). By combining the powerful reasoning and generative capabilities of LLMs with the timeliness and accuracy of external knowledge bases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a highly promising approach to addressing knowledge-intensive challenges in the operation and maintenance of electronic test instruments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of RAG and its applications in the field of electronic test instruments. First, the basic architecture of RAG is reviewed, including retrieval mechanisms, knowledge-base construction, and generative models. Then, considering the operational characteristics of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems, key knowledge-intensive tasks are analyzed, such as fault diagnosis, test configuration, and process planning, followed by a discussion of representative RAG-based applications, including intelligent fault diagnosis systems, adaptive test-parameter configuration, and interactive question-answering assistants. In addition, practical considerations for engineering implementation are discussed with respect to knowledge-base construction and effectiveness evaluation. Finally, open issues and future research directions are outlined, including multimodal RAG, federated learning for distributed knowledge bases, and edge deployment. This review aims to provide researchers and practitioners in relevant industries with a comprehensive understanding of the current status and development prospects of RAG technologies in electronic test instruments.

papers.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Systems: A Review of Methods, Benchmarks, Challenges and Future Directions
papers.venue: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports
papers.abstract: Aims: To critically review how machine learning is applied to predictive maintenance of industrial assets, to compare the main method families and benchmark practices, and to identify the barriers that limit industrial adoption and the priorities for future research. Study Design: Narrative (non-systematic) review. Methodology: Peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers and established review studies published between 2006 and 2026 were identified from major scientific databases and publisher platforms using combinations of the terms predictive maintenance, condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, prognostics, remaining useful life and machine learning. Seminal and highly cited works, benchmark-dataset papers and recent advances were prioritised. The evidence was synthesised by maintenance task, method family, dataset, evaluation metric and deployment issue. Results: Machine learning in predictive maintenance has progressed from feature-engineered shallow classifiers to deep convolutional, recurrent and attention-based networks that learn directly from raw sensor signals, and, more recently, to transfer learning, federated learning, physics-informed hybrid models and large foundation models. Deep models report strong accuracy on public benchmarks for bearing fault diagnosis and turbofan remaining-useful-life estimation, and hybrid physics and deep-learning models have extended prognostic horizons while requiring less training data. However, most evidence comes from a small number of laboratory or simulated datasets; performance under domain shift, scarce failure data, uncertainty quantification, interpretability and the link between prediction and maintenance decisions remain weakly addressed. Conclusion: Machine learning is a mature enabler of predictive maintenance, but industrial value depends less on marginal benchmark gains than on robust, explainable, uncertainty-aware and decision-oriented models validated on field data. Standardised evaluation protocols, open industrial datasets, hybrid knowledge-and-data models and cost-benefit evidence are the main priorities for future work.

papers.title_zh: 工业系统预测性维护中的机器学习：方法、基准、挑战与未来方向综述

article.lead: 预测维护模型在公开基准上表现出色，是否就能为工业设备创造实际价值？这篇综述梳理机器学习的方法演进与应用障碍，提醒读者把关注点从预测精度转向现场可靠性和维护决策。

sections.title: 从基准成绩走向工业维护价值
paragraphs: 工业资产的预测维护涉及状态监测、故障诊断和剩余使用寿命估计。本文关注的不只是哪些算法表现更好，还包括方法如何被评价，以及哪些障碍限制了工业采用。其核心问题是：模型的预测能力，怎样才能转化为可信、可用的维护依据？

sections.title: 以叙述性综述串联方法与部署问题
paragraphs: 本文采用叙述性、非系统性综述。作者从主要科学数据库和出版平台检索2006至2026年的同行评审期刊论文、会议论文及已有综述，组合使用预测维护、状态监测、故障诊断、预后、剩余使用寿命和机器学习等检索词。
文献选择优先考虑奠基性与高被引研究、基准数据集论文及近期进展，再按维护任务、方法类别、数据集、评价指标和部署问题综合证据。这是对既有研究的梳理，而非摘要报告的一项新模型实验。

sections.title: 模型持续演进，现场证据仍是关键短板
paragraphs: 综述概括的方法演进始于依赖人工特征的浅层分类器，随后发展为直接从原始传感器信号学习的卷积、循环及注意力网络，近期进一步扩展到迁移学习、联邦学习、物理信息混合模型和大型基础模型。
摘要报告，深度模型在轴承故障诊断和涡扇发动机剩余使用寿命估计的公开基准上取得较高准确性；物理与深度学习混合模型则延长了预测时间跨度，并减少了训练数据需求。但摘要没有给出对应的量化幅度或逐项比较条件。
与此同时，多数证据仍来自少数实验室或仿真数据集。领域偏移、故障数据稀缺、不确定性量化、可解释性，以及预测与维护决策之间的衔接，仍未得到充分解决。作者因此强调，工业价值不能仅由基准成绩的小幅提升来衡量。

sections.title: 摘要尚不能界定比较与验证范围
paragraphs: 仅凭本次摘要，无法判断纳入文献数量、各数据集的样本规模、具体模型的比较设置，以及现场验证覆盖了哪些设备和工况；也无法核对混合模型优势所对应的基线、指标和适用范围。这些信息是摘要未报告，并不意味着论文没有讨论或相关研究没有开展。

sections.title: 阅读启发：追问预测如何支持决策
paragraphs: 阅读启发：继续阅读时，可重点追问公开基准优势是否经现场数据验证，模型如何表达不确定性，以及预测输出怎样连接维护决策。摘要提出的标准化评价、开放工业数据、知识与数据混合模型及成本收益证据，可作为阅读线索，而不应被当作已经验证的落地成效。

papers.title: Thermal-Hydraulic Machine-Learning Surrogate Modeling for Structural Optimization of an Electric-Vehicle Battery Thermal Management System
papers.abstract: Abstract Structural design of battery thermal management systems requires prediction of maximum temperature, maximum temperature difference, and pressure drop, whose scales and response forms differ. Direct multioutput regression overlooks response differences and the data support of optimized designs. This study develops a response-aligned machine-learning surrogate coupled with coverage-constrained multi-objective optimization and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation. Screening ten regressors identifies Extra Trees as the thermal baseline and a multilayer perceptron for pressure drop. Nested fivefold cross-validation repeated over five seeds selects direct Extra Trees for maximum temperature, log-response Extra Trees for maximum temperature difference, and velocity-normalized pressure-drop reconstruction with a multilayer perceptron. A label-independent sampling rule adds 40 designs to the 80-sample modeling set, while a disjoint 40-design holdout evaluates the deterministic distributed thermal network (DTN) mapping. On this holdout, the log-response and velocity-normalized branches reduce root mean squared error by 10.48% and 24.76%, respectively; the 95% paired-bootstrap interval confirms the pressure-drop improvement. Nominal 90% cross-validation-plus intervals achieve empirical coverages of 87.5%, 90.0%, and 100% for the three outputs. Across resamples, contact-length ratio remains the highest-ranked thermal feature, and local parameter sweeps reproduce the DTN trends. With 10,000 evaluations, coverage-constrained nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II produces 334 nondominated solutions and contributes 99.1% of the combined front. Coverage-aware fuzzy evaluation selects a candidate with a score of 0.648; removing coverage changes the first-ranked design but retains nine of the top ten candidates. Within the DTN-defined domain, the framework enables structural screening and prioritizes candidates for physical validation.

papers.title_zh: 面向电动汽车电池热管理系统结构优化的热液机器学习代理建模

article.lead: 电动汽车电池热管理结构优化，不仅要预测温度与压降，还要判断优化方案是否得到已有数据支持。这项研究将响应差异、代理模型与覆盖约束结合起来，阅读价值在于理解：预测更准与候选设计更可信，如何共同进入优化流程。

sections.title: 温度与压降，不宜用同一种方式预测
paragraphs: 电池热管理结构设计需要同时关注最高温度、最大温差和压降，但这些输出的尺度与响应形式不同。摘要指出，直接采用多输出回归，会忽略响应差异以及优化设计的数据支撑。因此，研究既关注预测误差，也关注优化候选是否处于数据能够支持的范围。

sections.title: 按响应选择模型，再连接约束优化与评价
paragraphs: 研究筛选十种回归器，并通过跨五个随机种子重复的嵌套五折交叉验证，选择三条预测分支：最高温度采用直接 Extra Trees 回归；最大温差采用对数响应 Extra Trees；压降采用速度归一化重构与多层感知机。
与标签无关的采样规则向含80个样本的建模集补充40个设计，另用互不重叠的40个设计检验确定性分布式热网络（DTN）映射。代理模型随后连接带覆盖约束的多目标优化与模糊综合评价，用于生成并筛选候选结构。

sections.title: 误差有所下降，覆盖信息也影响设计排序
paragraphs: 在留出集上，对数响应与速度归一化分支的均方根误差分别降低10.48%和24.76%；95%配对自助法区间支持压降预测的改进。名义覆盖率为90%的交叉验证加法预测区间，对三个输出的实际覆盖率依次为87.5%、90.0%和100%。
重采样中，接触长度比始终是排名最高的热学特征，局部参数扫描也复现了DTN趋势。经过10,000次评估，带覆盖约束的非支配排序遗传算法II得到334个非支配解，占合并前沿的99.1%。
考虑覆盖信息的模糊评价选出得分为0.648的候选。移除覆盖因素后，首位设计改变，但前十名中仍保留九个候选。这说明覆盖信息会影响最终优先级，却不能据此认定所选结构已经获得物理性能验证。

sections.title: 验证边界仍是DTN定义的设计域
paragraphs: 摘要将适用范围限定在DTN定义的域内，所报告的留出检验针对该确定性映射，不能直接等同于真实电池系统验证。摘要未交代具体几何与工况范围、误差降幅对应的详细比较基线，以及合并前沿包含哪些比较方法；实物验证范围也无法由摘要判断，需进一步阅读原文。

sections.title: 阅读启发：区分预测准确与设计可信
paragraphs: 阅读启发：结构优化中的代理模型，不应只看误差指标，也值得追问候选方案的数据支撑。进一步阅读时，可重点核对覆盖约束如何定义、如何进入优化与评价，以及预测区间覆盖率和设计域覆盖约束分别表达什么。当前资料支持将该框架理解为结构筛选工具，而非已完成物理验证的设计结论。
